root_idea.summary: The root has two principal semantic orientations: constriction or straitness, and illness.
root_idea.development: The constriction branch extends from narrowness of place to straitened life, sustenance, and hardship. A distinct branch denotes coryza and disease; other Classical derivatives attest compactness, firmness, and weakness without collapsing them into the Qur'anic adjective.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-attested adjective is displayed under the normalized citation form ضَنْكٌ rather than the accusative occurrence form ضَنْكًا.

senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction مَعِيشَةً ضَنْكًا, it describes a constricted or difficult life or means of subsistence.

senses.definition: Unlawful or forbidden, specifically of livelihood.
senses.usage_conditions: A reported interpretation of مَعِيشَةً ضَنْكًا understands the expression as forbidden livelihood or gain, even when materially abundant; this is a specialized interpretation alongside the basic sense of straitness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become narrow or strait; narrowness, straitness, and hardship.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb is used of a place becoming narrow; related nominal and adjectival forms describe narrow places, constricted life or sustenance, and narrow things generally.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be weak in body, intellect, judgment, or soul; weak in those respects.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a person or to the corresponding adjectival description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become thick, gathered together, and dense.
To become afflicted with coryza or a discharge from the head and nose.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes the person affected by the nasal illness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause someone to be afflicted with coryza or nasal discharge.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative construction referring to causing another person to suffer the illness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Coryza, or a defluxion from the head and nose.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for the nasal illness also called zukām.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Compact, plump, or firmly built, with abundant flesh; robust or large in build.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to people, camels, and trees; of a she-camel it can refer particularly to a thick hind part, and of trees to substantial size.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Affected by a constant or chronic pervasive disease, or emaciated by disease to the point of death.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes a person whose bodily condition has been severely affected by illness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Affected by the illness called ضُنَاكٌ, coryza.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive description of someone suffering from that nasal illness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A servant who works for his bread.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized social description of a person supporting himself through such service.
Reported as an equivalent of مَقْطُوعٌ.

cautions: The sole Quran occurrence is the adjective ضَنْكًا in a livelihood construction; the public headword is normalized to the citation form ضَنْكٌ.

The Quranic phrase has competing exegetical readings, including punishment of the grave and Hell. These are treated as interpretations of the phrase rather than additional lexical senses; forbidden livelihood is retained as a separately reported lexical specialization.
